notes: the quantum histogram samples A directly (k = 0); like the classical one it converges as 1/sqrt(N): it validates that the circuit encodes the same physics and is not speedup evidence
agreement is judged by chi-square sums over 17 categories; per-row z-scores are not used
both samples go through the same mc_lattice.sample_exit_rows: the lattice engine's 11-bit strings and the Q1 count keys (int(key, 2) & 0x7FF, key character 0 = flag qubit 11)
outside_support counts shots on zero-amplitude strings and flag_mismatch shots whose flag disagrees with the string's transmitted predicate; both are 0 for an ideal simulator
chi-square: two-sample sum (c - q)^2 / (c + q) for equal totals; goodness of fit sum (c - S p)^2 / (S p) against exact.exit_row_distribution_k1; acceptance bound dof + 5 sqrt(2 dof)
sampling complexity only: this figure makes no speedup or wall-clock claim

parameters.seeding: root = SeedSequence(seed); classical, rows, aer = root.spawn(3); classical = run_lattice(kernels, S, classical); quantum rows = sample_exit_rows(kernels, strings, rows) with the Aer count keys sorted ascending and expanded by np.repeat; seed_simulator = aer.generate_state(1, uint32)[0]
